modules.title: Software Testing

modules.title: Project Management
modules.description: Estimation techniques, scheduling, risk management, and configuration management.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the differences between Waterfall and Agile models.
importantQuestions.answer: Waterfall is sequential (requirements → design → code → test → deploy) with no going back. Agile is iterative, delivering working software in 2-4 week sprints with continuous feedback. Waterfall suits well-defined projects; Agile handles changing requirements.

importantQuestions.question: What is an SRS document? List its components.
importantQuestions.answer: Software Requirements Specification (SRS) formally documents all functional and non-functional requirements. Components: Introduction, Overall Description, Specific Requirements (functional, performance, design constraints), External Interface Requirements, and Appendices.

importantQuestions.question: Describe the SOLID principles in software design.
importantQuestions.answer: S: Single Responsibility — one class, one job. O: Open/Closed — open for extension, closed for modification. L: Liskov Substitution — subtypes must be substitutable. I: Interface Segregation — many specific interfaces > one general. D: Dependency Inversion — depend on abstractions.

importantQuestions.question: Compare Black Box and White Box testing.
importantQuestions.answer: Black Box: tests functionality without knowing internal code (equivalence partitioning, boundary value). White Box: tests internal logic with code knowledge (statement, branch, path coverage). Both are essential for comprehensive testing.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the COCOMO estimation model.
importantQuestions.answer: Constructive Cost Model estimates effort (person-months) and schedule from project size (KLOC). Three levels: Basic (effort = a × KLOC^b), Intermediate (adds cost drivers), Detailed (phase-level estimation). Organic, semi-detached, and embedded project types.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the three-schema architecture of DBMS.
importantQuestions.answer: External Schema (user views), Conceptual Schema (logical structure of entire DB), Internal Schema (physical storage). Provides data independence — changes at one level don't affect others.

importantQuestions.question: Write SQL for the following: Find employees earning more than the average salary.
importantQuestions.answer: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

importantQuestions.question: Differentiate between 3NF and BCNF.
importantQuestions.answer: 3NF: For every FD X→Y, either X is a superkey OR Y is a prime attribute. BCNF: For every FD X→Y, X must be a superkey (stricter). BCNF eliminates all redundancy from FDs but may lose dependency preservation.

importantQuestions.question: Explain Two-Phase Locking protocol.
importantQuestions.answer: Growing Phase: transaction acquires locks, no releases. Shrinking Phase: transaction releases locks, no new acquisitions. Guarantees serializability but may cause deadlocks. Strict 2PL holds all exclusive locks until commit.

importantQuestions.question: Compare stack and queue data structures.
importantQuestions.answer: Stack: LIFO (Last In First Out), push/pop at top. Queue: FIFO (First In First Out), enqueue at rear, dequeue at front. Stack uses: function calls, undo. Queue uses: BFS, scheduling.

importantQuestions.question: Explain AVL tree rotations.
importantQuestions.answer: AVL trees maintain balance factor (-1, 0, 1) at every node. Four rotations: LL (right rotate), RR (left rotate), LR (left-right rotate), RL (right-left rotate). Time complexity for all ops: O(log n).

importantQuestions.question: Compare BFS and DFS traversals.
importantQuestions.answer: BFS: Level-order using queue, finds shortest path in unweighted graphs, O(V+E). DFS: Depth-first using stack/recursion, used for cycle detection and topological sort, O(V+E).

importantQuestions.question: Explain the concept of Dynamic Programming with an example.
importantQuestions.answer: DP solves problems by breaking into overlapping subproblems and storing results (memoization/tabulation). Example: Fibonacci — fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2). Without DP: O(2^n). With DP: O(n).

importantQuestions.question: Simplify F(A,B,C) = Σm(0,1,2,5,7) using K-Map.
importantQuestions.answer: Group: m(0,1) → A'B', m(5,7) → AC, m(1,5) → B'C. Result: F = A'B' + AC + B'C (or further simplified).

importantQuestions.question: Design a 4-bit binary adder using full adders.
importantQuestions.answer: Cascade 4 full adders: C_out of each stage connects to C_in of next. First C_in = 0 for addition. Produces 4-bit sum + carry out. Ripple carry adder with propagation delay of 4 × gate_delay.

importantQuestions.question: Compare Mealy and Moore state machines.
importantQuestions.answer: Moore: outputs depend only on current state (output on state). Mealy: outputs depend on current state AND inputs (output on transitions). Moore needs more states but is simpler; Mealy responds faster.

importantQuestions.question: Compare preemptive and non-preemptive scheduling.
importantQuestions.answer: Preemptive: OS can interrupt a running process (RR, SRTF, Priority Preemptive). Non-preemptive: process runs until completion or voluntary yield (FCFS, SJF). Preemptive provides better response time; non-preemptive is simpler.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the Banker's Algorithm with an example.
importantQuestions.answer: Safety algorithm checks if a safe sequence exists. For each process, check if Need ≤ Available. If yes, allocate, run, release resources. If all processes can finish, state is safe. Prevents deadlock by refusing unsafe requests.

importantQuestions.question: Compare FIFO, LRU, and Optimal page replacement.
importantQuestions.answer: FIFO: replace oldest page, simple but Belady's anomaly. LRU: replace least recently used, good performance, O(n) or hardware support needed. Optimal: replace page not used for longest future time — theoretical best, not implementable.

importantQuestions.question: Compare OSI and TCP/IP models.
importantQuestions.answer: OSI: 7 layers (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application) — theoretical reference model. TCP/IP: 4 layers (Network Access, Internet, Transport, Application) — practical implementation. TCP/IP merges top 3 OSI layers.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the TCP three-way handshake.
importantQuestions.answer: 1) Client sends SYN (seq=x). 2) Server responds SYN-ACK (seq=y, ack=x+1). 3) Client sends ACK (ack=y+1). Connection established. Ensures both sides agree on sequence numbers. Four-way handshake for termination (FIN/ACK).

importantQuestions.question: Subnet the network 192.168.1.0/24 into 4 subnets.

importantQuestions.question: Convert the NFA to DFA for the language accepting strings ending in '01'.
importantQuestions.answer: States: {q0}, {q0,q1}, {q0,q2}. On 0: {q0}→{q0,q1}. On 1: {q0}→{q0}, {q0,q1}→{q0,q2}. Accept state: {q0,q2}. Apply subset construction for all reachable states.

importantQuestions.question: Use Pumping Lemma to prove L = {a^n b^n} is not regular.
importantQuestions.answer: Assume regular with pumping length p. Choose w = a^p b^p. For any split w = xyz with |xy| ≤ p, y = a^k (k≥1). Pumping: xy²z = a^(p+k) b^p ∉ L. Contradiction. Therefore not regular.

importantQuestions.question: What is the significance of the Halting Problem?
importantQuestions.answer: The Halting Problem asks: does a given TM halt on a given input? Turing proved it's undecidable (no algorithm can solve it for all cases) using diagonalization. Establishes fundamental limits of computation — not everything is computable.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the properties of LTI systems.
importantQuestions.answer: Linearity: superposition holds (scaling + additivity). Time-Invariance: shifting input shifts output by same amount. Output = input * impulse response (convolution). Completely characterized by h(t) or H(s).

importantQuestions.question: State and prove the time-shifting property of Fourier Transform.
importantQuestions.answer: If x(t) ↔ X(jω), then x(t-t₀) ↔ e^(-jωt₀) X(jω). Proof: FT of x(t-t₀) = ∫x(t-t₀)e^(-jωt)dt. Substitute τ=t-t₀: = e^(-jωt₀) ∫x(τ)e^(-jωτ)dτ = e^(-jωt₀) X(jω).

importantQuestions.question: State and explain the Second Law of Thermodynamics.
importantQuestions.answer: Kelvin-Planck: Impossible to convert all heat from a reservoir to work in a cycle. Clausius: Heat cannot flow from cold to hot body without external work. Both are equivalent and establish the direction of natural processes and concept of entropy.

importantQuestions.question: Compare Otto and Diesel cycles.
importantQuestions.answer: Otto: constant-volume heat addition, spark ignition, compression ratio 6-10, efficiency = 1-(1/r^(γ-1)). Diesel: constant-pressure heat addition, compression ignition, ratio 14-22, higher efficiency but complex. Otto used in petrol engines, Diesel in diesel engines.

importantQuestions.question: Explain A* search algorithm with admissibility condition.
importantQuestions.answer: A* uses f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g = cost so far, h = heuristic estimate to goal. Admissible: h never overestimates actual cost. A* is optimal and complete when h is admissible. Time/space: O(b^d).

importantQuestions.question: Compare supervised and unsupervised learning.
importantQuestions.answer: Supervised: labeled data, learns input→output mapping (classification, regression). Examples: Decision Trees, SVM. Unsupervised: no labels, finds patterns/structure (clustering, dimensionality reduction). Examples: K-Means, PCA.

importantQuestions.question: Prove by induction: 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2.
importantQuestions.answer: Base: n=1, LHS=1, RHS=1(2)/2=1. ✓ Inductive step: Assume true for k. Then 1+...+k+(k+1) = k(k+1)/2 + (k+1) = (k+1)(k+2)/2. True for k+1. By induction, true for all n≥1.

importantQuestions.question: State and prove the Pigeonhole Principle.
importantQuestions.answer: If n items are placed in m containers and n > m, then at least one container has more than one item. Proof by contradiction: if each container has ≤1 item, total items ≤ m < n. Contradiction.

importantQuestions.question: Compare IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS with examples.
importantQuestions.answer: IaaS: Infrastructure (VMs, storage) — AWS EC2, GCP Compute. PaaS: Platform (runtime, DB) — Heroku, Google App Engine. SaaS: Complete apps — Gmail, Salesforce. Abstraction increases from IaaS→SaaS; user control decreases.

importantQuestions.question: Compare VMs and Containers.
importantQuestions.answer: VMs: full OS per VM, hypervisor-based, heavier (GBs), slower boot. Containers: share host OS kernel, lighter (MBs), faster boot, Docker/K8s. Containers for microservices; VMs for full isolation.

importantQuestions.question: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff.
importantQuestions.answer: Bias: error from overly simple models (underfitting). Variance: error from overly complex models (overfitting). Total Error = Bias² + Variance + Noise. Goal: find sweet spot. Regularization reduces variance at slight increase in bias.

importantQuestions.question: How does SVM find the optimal hyperplane?
importantQuestions.answer: SVM maximizes the margin between classes. Support vectors are closest points to the decision boundary. Optimization: minimize ||w||² subject to yᵢ(w·xᵢ+b) ≥ 1. Kernel trick maps to higher dimensions for non-linear separation.

importantQuestions.question: Derive Bernoulli's equation from Euler's equation.
importantQuestions.answer: Along a streamline: dp/ρ + VdV + gdz = 0 (Euler). Integrate for incompressible flow: P/ρ + V²/2 + gz = constant. Assumptions: steady, incompressible, inviscid, along streamline.

importantQuestions.question: Explain Reynolds number and its significance.
importantQuestions.answer: Re = ρVD/μ = Inertial forces/Viscous forces. Re < 2300: laminar flow (orderly). Re > 4000: turbulent (chaotic). 2300-4000: transitional. Critical for predicting flow behavior and calculating friction losses.

importantQuestions.question: Construct LL(1) parsing table for a given grammar.
importantQuestions.answer: Steps: 1) Eliminate left recursion. 2) Left factor. 3) Compute FIRST and FOLLOW sets. 4) For each production A→α, add to M[A, a] for each a in FIRST(α). If ε in FIRST(α), add for each b in FOLLOW(A). No conflicts = LL(1).

importantQuestions.question: Generate three-address code for: a = b * -c + b * -c.
importantQuestions.answer: t1 = minus c; t2 = b * t1; t3 = minus c; t4 = b * t3; t5 = t2 + t4; a = t5. With DAG optimization: t1 = minus c; t2 = b * t1; t3 = t2 + t2; a = t3 (CSE eliminated).

importantQuestions.question: Explain the architecture of 8086 microprocessor.
importantQuestions.answer: Two units: BIU (Bus Interface Unit — fetches instructions, manages bus) and EU (Execution Unit — decodes and executes). 20-bit address bus (1MB), 16-bit data bus. Segmented memory: CS, DS, SS, ES. Instruction queue for pipelining.

importantQuestions.question: Compare 8086 and 8051.
importantQuestions.answer: 8086: microprocessor, 16-bit, external memory/peripherals needed, general purpose. 8051: microcontroller, 8-bit, built-in RAM/ROM/timers/serial/ports, embedded applications. 8051 is self-contained; 8086 needs external chips.

importantQuestions.question: Explain RSA algorithm with an example.
importantQuestions.answer: Key gen: Choose p=3, q=11. n=33, φ=20. Choose e=7 (gcd(7,20)=1). d=3 (7×3 mod 20=1). Public: (33,7), Private: (33,3). Encrypt M=2: C=2⁷ mod 33=29. Decrypt: M=29³ mod 33=2. Security based on factoring difficulty.

importantQuestions.question: Compare symmetric and asymmetric encryption.
importantQuestions.answer: Symmetric: same key for encrypt/decrypt, fast, key distribution problem (DES, AES). Asymmetric: public/private key pair, slower, solves key distribution (RSA, ECC). Hybrid approach: use asymmetric for key exchange, symmetric for data.

importantQuestions.question: Explain React component lifecycle and hooks.
importantQuestions.answer: Class lifecycle: mounting (constructor, render, componentDidMount), updating (shouldComponentUpdate, render, componentDidUpdate), unmounting (componentWillUnmount). Hooks equivalent: useState for state, useEffect for lifecycle, useContext for context, useMemo for optimization.

importantQuestions.question: Design a REST API for a blog application.
importantQuestions.answer: GET /api/posts — list all. GET /api/posts/:id — get one. POST /api/posts — create (auth required). PUT /api/posts/:id — update. DELETE /api/posts/:id — delete. Use proper HTTP status codes (200, 201, 404, 500).
